Disclaimer: I am in no way justifying, or condoning pressuring anyone for sex in any situation, in any way. That being said:

What happens after the honeymoon period when one person still desires sex, but their partner has lost interest (commonly referred to as a dead bedroom)?

I think it's still the duty of the disinterested party to at least minimally fulfill the sexual needs of their partner, if sustaining the relationship is a priority. In bullet form, here's why:

  • Each partner in the relationship is the others' only source of intimacy and sex (assuming a monogamous relationship), therefore if one partner withholds sex, the physical needs of the other is not being met. What is ultimately a chore or an inconvenience for one partner is a physiological necessity for the other.

  • Compromise is fundamentally part of every aspect of a relationship, and sex is no different. I'm conflicted in my thinking on this point: No one should be made to have sex if they don't want to. However, both my SO and I do things for each other that we don't necessarily want to do because it's better for the relationship, or it makes the other happy. I don't believe sex and intimacy should be treated differently- it's reasonable to have expectations of sex as a requirement of the relationship.

Thoughts?
CMV: In an intimate relationship, you have an obligation to satisfy your partner's sexual needs.
The question remains how often should one side have intimacy and sex with his/her SO. If someone doesn't want to have sex should she do it every day for her SO. Where do we draw the line?

That goes along with my second point: Sex should be up for compromise. I want sex every day, but you want sex never? Let's have sex once a week. I think that's a reasonable compromise that obligates both parties to sex.
My point is where do you make a line. If one has a sex drive of twice a day. How do you compromise on that.

That's not for me to say- it would be up to the couple. But I feel that both partners have an obligation to make sure the minimum sexual needs of their partner is filled- however that compromise comes about.

If someone doesn't want to have sex should she do it every day for her SO.

I'd say yeah. When you love someone, you're signing up for all the shit that comes with that person.

I'll keep this brief, as it increasingly seems like I am becoming but a drop amongst buckets of great thinkers, critics, artists, innovators and creators and debaters (dare I say, master debaters?)

Here we are lasses and lads: A dawn where individuals in Sweden can write, in the same language no less, words that inspire other individuals in Brazil, and Australia, and in America, the land who's stars I gaze upon now. Finally, we live in a time where a lone voice can reach out across oceans and time zones, and not only find others who share that same passion, but find people who are happy to assist another in their pursuit of betterment. Truly, what a time to be alive! Also, everyone in every other country around the globe, sorry about all my countrymen who come up to you and think they can bridge existing language barriers by repeating what they just said, again in English, only louder and slower. We Americans are a silly bunch sometimes...

Myself? I'm a young, white male in that country under the night sky, so I apologize in advance for any prejudices or biases, intentional or unintentional, that may seep into my future messages. Like many people who frequent sites like this, I lurked for years, eager to learn untold treasures from the world we share, and contributing my own voice to this great din of humanity rarely. When I do speak, I want it known that it comes from a place of passion, and more importantly, always intended to promote and encourage conversation; never, Never to scold, insult, demean or belittle.

So, friends and strangers; brothers and sisters, mothers and fathers; wise elders and you young damn kids who keep going on old people's lawns: There's a great deal we can all learn, and wonders unimaginable we've yet to witness in our time ahead. But in times both hard and golden, today, take refuge in what we can accomplish together, now that "together" finally is no longer limited by borders on a map.

Let's have ourselves a chat.

For me, I try not to seek the feeling. I think of pride as more of a reflective indulgence. While it's nice to feel proud about an accomplishment or where you're at in life, ultimately it doesn't do anything for you, and can cause you to become arrogant. I try to focus on just doing the next thing on my list. I like how Voltaire ends Candide with "we must cultivate our garden," which is his answer to the questions of optimism, pessimism and how we should feel about the world around us. What I took from it is that we should simply work to be productive and for our enjoyment rather than dwell on complex emotions and states of mind.

But if you meant to ask what we do that we are proud about, then I'd have to say I have an uncanny ability to pick things up with my toes.

By being calm, level headed, and stoic. Being proud usually means I kicked ass and have a license to act as cool as I feel.
